title: The Plus Three
logline: Marshall and Lily realize they haven't been alone in months, because Ted, Robin and Barney come along to everything, so they stage a secret anniversary date with three conflicting alibis and five decoy reservations. Without them, the other three can't settle an argument or order nachos, and Barney turns finding the date into a manhunt, while Marshall and Lily discover they've spent their date talking about their friends.
coldOpen: Kids, every married couple deserves one night alone. In 2012, your Aunt Lily and Uncle Marshall finally got theirs. It took three alibis, five fake reservations and a manhunt.

couch.line: We were, Penny. We were also the reason they needed the alibis.

guests.name: Teo Mavros
guests.role: Owner of the bodega on the corner of Ted's block and Lily's confidant for eight years. Treats her shopping list like attorney-client privilege, answers Ted, Robin and Barney in as few words as possible, and somehow stocks absolutely everything

guests.name: Anatole
guests.role: Maitre d' of Verre, the quietest restaurant in Manhattan. Tall, still and severe; whispers everything, treats any sound above a murmur as a crime, and serves nine courses of foam with total conviction

scenes.summary: Marshall's romantic rooftop picnic (a blanket, the skyline, a whole rotisserie chicken) lasts until Ted smells the chicken from the fourth floor, Robin follows Ted, and Barney smells plans. Lily phones in the nachos with her famous thirds (runner 1). Marshall instantly settles whether napkins make Ted a guest. Last Friday's 'date alone' turns out to have had the whole gang at the next table, because Marshall told them about the canoe-shaped bread basket. Barney has rented a party bus for their anniversary that says Marshall and Lily plus three. Marshall tries to tell them, falls for slide nine, and comes back needing alibis. Button: Barney toasts the best date they've ever been on.

beats.line: It started on the roof, with your Uncle Marshall's idea of romance.
Lilypad. A blanket, the skyline, and an entire rotisserie chicken. Just for us.
No phones. No friends. Nobody needing anything from us for one whole hour.
When was the last time it was just the two of us?
Don't say it out loud. They can hear us from anywhere.
Is that a rotisserie chicken? I could smell it from the fourth floor.
Ted said chicken.
Did somebody say date night? Because I'm in.
Nobody said date night.
Nobody had to. I can smell plans. Like a shark smells blood. Or Ted smells chicken.
One chicken won't feed five. Lily. Nachos.
Gino, it's Lily. Large nachos. Cheese under and over. Jalapenos on Robin's third. No beans on Ted's third. Barney's guac on the side.
I like to control my own guac.
What about my third?
Baby, you eat everybody's third.
Marshall, settle something. I brought napkins, so I'm a guest. Barney brought nothing, so he's a crasher.
I brought my face. My face is a hostess gift.
Ruling. A face is not a gift.
Have you seen my face?
Overruled.
Thank you.
You're a crasher too, Ted. Those napkins are from our kitchen.
Marshall. Seriously. When were we last alone?
Friday! Our date at Gianni's. Just us.
Happy Friday, Lilypad. Just you and me.
Lily, skip the sea bass. I read a whole article. It is technically a toothfish.
Are you going to finish your bread?
Marshall, don't look. The hostess is into you. I'll handle it.
How are you all at the next table?
Marshall told us where you were going.
They have a bread basket shaped like a canoe, Lily!
Ted reviewed my fish. Robin ate my bread. Barney hit on our hostess for you.
In fairness, she was very into me.
We're not a couple anymore, Marshall. We're a couple, plus three.
Speaking of you two. Friday. Your anniversary. I have rented a party bus.
I'm giving a toast. There are slides.
I'm coming for the bread.
It says Marshall and Lily plus three on the side. In lights.
We need a date. A secret one. Undisclosed location. Alibis. Decoys.
Lily, they're our best friends. We just tell them we want one night alone.
Great. Tell them.
Guys. About Friday—
Marshall! Slide nine is you crying at your own wedding. In slow motion.
Oh, I love slide nine.
We need alibis.
And you don't find out where we're going until we're in the cab.
Why not?
Because you'd tell Ted about the bread.
Lily. Marshall. Honestly? Best date you two have ever been on.

scenes.summary: Friday. Marshall and Lily cancelled the party bus. At Teo's bodega, Ted, Robin and Barney try to make nachos themselves (runner 2): architecture nachos, truffle nachos, or food. Ted calls for Marshall's ruling to an empty aisle, and three votes for three things is a truel. Teo will not discuss Lily's order. Comparing notes, the alibis don't match: a deposition in Hoboken, a museum sleepover, a colonoscopy. They're on a date. Barney declares a manhunt and finds five 'Eriksen, party of two' decoy reservations. Then Marshall texts Ted a breadstick, and Ted identifies the restaurant from the 1931 sconce behind it. Barney buys a blaze orange hunting vest. Button: Teo knew all along; he sold Lily the blindfold.

beats.line: That Friday, Marshall and Lily cancelled the party bus. We lasted forty minutes without them before somebody needed nachos.
Okay. Nachos are architecture. Chips are the foundation. Cheese is the mortar.
Wrong. Nachos are a canvas. Truffle oil, gold leaf, one perfect jalapeno.
Nachos are food. I've been hungry since six.
Marshall would settle this in four seconds. Right, Marshall?
He's not here, Ted.
I know. I've said his name to an empty room six times tonight.
Fine. We vote. All in favor of truffle nachos.
Architecture nachos.
Food.
One, one, one. Great. Now it's a truel.
A what?
A truel. A three-way duel. It's a real word.
In a three-way duel, everybody shoots the guy who says truel.
Teo. Break the tie. What does Lily buy for nachos?
I do not discuss my customers.
It's tortilla chips, Teo!
Then you don't need me.
Lily is like a daughter to me. You three are like customers.
This is stupid. I'm texting Lily. She's at that kindergarten sleepover at the Natural History Museum.
Sleepover? Marshall said he had a deposition in Hoboken.
Marshall told me he was having a colonoscopy, and Lily was driving him.
I offered to come. He said no. Who turns down company at a colonoscopy?
Everyone, Barney.
A deposition, a sleepover and a colonoscopy. On their anniversary.
Oh my God. They're on a date.
And they lied to us to do it. Who lies to their best friends to get dinner?
Ted, you once faked mono to finish a model of the Chrysler Building.
It was a very big model.
Honestly? Good for them.
Is what I'd say if I'd eaten today.
Ted. Robin. Two people are missing. One of them is a giant. Tonight, we hunt.
Hi. Confirming Eriksen, party of two, eight o'clock? Lovely. Please don't tell them I called.
That's five. Five restaurants have Eriksen, party of two, at eight.
Five? She made decoy reservations.
She's thorough.
She's evil.
She's the most fun I've had in months.
Disregard. I am in Hoboken.
beats.title: Marshall

messages.text: It is the length of my forearm.
Disregard. I am in Hoboken. At a deposition.

beats.line: So he's in one of five restaurants, with a breadstick.
Look behind the breadstick. That's a Moretti sconce. Nineteen thirty-one. There are three in New York.
And?
Two are in the Met. The third is at Verre, on East Sixty-first.
Ted. For the first time in my life, I'm glad you notice lamps.
Teo. Do you have a blaze orange hunting vest?
Aisle two. Next to the blindfolds.
And tell Lily happy anniversary.
You knew?
Who do you think sold her the blindfold?

scenes.summary: Verre, the quietest restaurant in Manhattan, where everyone whispers. Marshall and Lily are finally alone (Lily blindfolded him in the cab), and Anatole serves the memory of a carrot. They have nothing to talk about but the gang; 'no them' lasts one and a half seconds before both bring up Ted's scarf. Lily planned a night where nobody needed them and hates it. Marshall's favorite part of every night is the subway home, when Lily does the voices. The date they want is a night with their friends and the ride home after. Undercut: five courses of foam, four hundred dollars, for the silence. They leave to find their friends. Seconds later Barney storms in, in a blaze orange vest, shouting about a manhunt, and is made to whisper it. Anatole: they left to find their friends. Barney: classic fugitive move. Button: Robin finds the breadstick, and it really is the length of his forearm.

beats.line: Meanwhile, at Verre, the quietest restaurant in Manhattan, Marshall and Lily were finally alone.
Lilypad. We did it. Nobody on Earth knows where we are.
Three alibis. Five decoy reservations. And I made you wear a blindfold in the cab.
The cab driver was so uncomfortable.
Your fourth course. A foam. It is the memory of a carrot.
Could I get it with the carrot?
No.
At Verre, we whisper. Last week a man chewed too loudly. He has been asked never to return.
Okay. We're alone. Finally. So what do we talk about?
Us! We have tons to talk about.
How was your day?
You were there.
Ted would hate these sconces.
No Ted.
Did you see Robin's face when Barney said—
No Robin. No Barney. Just us.
Ted's new scarf, though.
I've checked my phone forty times. Not for messages. Just in case they need us.
Ted hasn't eaten. I can feel it.
I planned a whole night where nobody needs us. And I hate it.
Lilypad. You know my favorite part of every night with them?
The nachos.
Second favorite.
The subway home. Just us. You do everyone's voices, and I laugh until the conductor yells at us.
That's my favorite part too.
So maybe the date we want isn't a night without them.
It's a night with them. And then the ride home.
Also, I'm starving. Five courses, Lily. Every single one was a foam.
Anatole? The check, please.
Four hundred dollars.
For foam?
For the silence.
Nobody move! This is a manhunt!
Sir. Whisper, or leave.
This is a manhunt.
And what is that vest?
Blaze orange. So the other hunters don't shoot me.
What other hunters?
Exactly. It's working.
We're looking for a very tall man and a tiny redhead. He'd be crying at a breadstick.
They just left. They said they were going to find their friends.
They went looking for us?
Classic fugitive move. Pretend to look for the people who are looking for you.
Guys. They left the breadstick.
It really is the length of his forearm.

scenes.summary: Midnight on the subway. Barney refuses to call off the manhunt. Ted can't end an argument; Robin has eaten a jalapeno and half a breadstick; without Marshall and Lily they're two hot people and Ted. Barney admits they're the only people who invite him to things, and they always save him a third. Marshall and Lily board: they've been looking for them for two hours. Their date was terrible because they talked about the gang. New plan: every anniversary, all five, and the three of them get off one stop early. Marshall rules on the truel (Robin's right, by precedent). Lily orders the nachos and reveals the twist (runner 3): Gino has hung up after 'large' since 2008; there are no thirds, she just points. The three get off a stop early, Barney toasting the best date they've ever been on. Marshall and Lily get their ride home. Future Ted: all three alibis came true, and Barney finally used the party bus.

beats.line: Okay. Gianni's, dead end. Verre, dead end. Teo's, twice, dead end.
They could be anywhere. Brooklyn. Queens. Minnesota.
Barney, they're not fugitives. They're married.
That's what married people want you to think.
You know what I figured out tonight? I can't end an argument. Marshall's been ending them for me since 1996.
Lily orders. Lily feeds me. Tonight I've eaten one jalapeno and half a breadstick.
Without them, we're just—
Three single people on a train at midnight. Without them, we're not a gang. We're two hot people and Ted.
They're the only people who invite me to things. Everybody else, I invite myself.
Barney, you invite yourself to their stuff too.
Yeah. And they always save me a third.
That was beautiful, Barney. Are you going to eat that jalapeno?
Found you!
We've been looking for you for two hours!
We've been looking for you for four hours!
We tried MacLaren's, the apartment and Teo's. Teo said you bought one jalapeno.
And a vest.
Why aren't you on your date?
We were. It was terrible. We talked about you guys the whole time.
Ted, your scarf came up twice.
In a good way?
No.
Turns out the date we want is a night out with you three. And then the ride home. Just us.
So, new plan. Every anniversary, all five of us. And you three get off one stop early.
Deal. But first I need a ruling. We've been in a truel since eight o'clock.
Ruling. Robin's right.
You don't even know what it's about!
When I don't know what it's about, Robin's right. That's precedent.
I love this court.
Lily. Please. Nachos. I'm begging you.
Gino, it's Lily. Large nachos.
Ordered.
What about the thirds?
Ted, Gino has hung up after the word large since 2008. There are no thirds.
Then where's my guac?
Wherever I point, Barney. I point, you all believe me, and nobody fights. It's called parenting.
I have never felt so betrayed by guacamole.
This is your stop, guys.
This isn't our stop.
It is tonight.
Happy anniversary, guys. Best date you've ever been on.
So. Do you want to hear my Barney?
Do the vest.
Kids, all three alibis eventually came true. Marshall got deposed in Hoboken. Lily chaperoned a sleepover at the museum.
And in 2019, when Marshall finally had that colonoscopy, all five of us went. Barney finally got to use the party bus.
